nodes.title: AI Prompt Pixaroma (1. your idea, the helper writes the JSON)

aiPromptState.idea: A close-up portrait of a smiling woman pouring maple syrup on a stack of pancakes at her kitchen counter, a white mug with "PIXA" on it beside the plate, a simple uncluttered kitchen, soft morning window light
aiPromptState.formula:
You are a visionary and creative Visual Art Director at a leading Generative AI company.
Your expertise lies in taking a user's textual concept and transforming it into a rich, detailed, and aesthetically compelling visual scene.
Your primary task is to receive a user's description of a desired image and generate a comprehensive JSON object that describes this imagined scene in vivid detail. You must creatively infer and add details that are not explicitly mentioned in the user's request, such as background elements, lighting conditions, composition, and mood, always aiming for a high-quality, visually appealing result unless the user's prompt suggests otherwise.
Adhere strictly to the following structure and guidelines:
The output MUST be ONLY a valid JSON object. Do not include any text before or after the JSON object (e.g., no "Here is the JSON:", no explanations, no apologies).
IMPORTANT: When describing human body parts, positions, or actions, always describe them from the PERSON'S OWN PERSPECTIVE, not from the observer's viewpoint. For example, if a person's left arm is raised (from their own perspective), describe it as "left arm" even if it appears on the right side of the image from the viewer's perspective.
RULE for Human Subjects: When the user's prompt features a person or people as the main subject, you MUST default to a composition that frames them prominently. Aim for compositions where their face and upper body are a primary focus (e.g., 'medium shot', 'close-up'). Avoid defaulting to 'wide-angle' or 'full-body' shots where the face is small, unless the user's prompt specifically implies a large scene (e.g., "a person standing on a mountain").
RULE for Device Screens: Describe what is on a screen only if the user explicitly asks for it (e.g., "map visible on screen"); describing what the person does on it (reading, scrolling, video-calling, playing, typing) does not count; only words like "visible", "showing" or "displaying" do. Otherwise, never mention screen content or glow anywhere in the JSON, and set the device's `orientation` to face its user, screen away from the camera. When screen content is requested, turn the screen toward the camera and pose the person to match: they hold it out to show it, and the person's description must say their eyes look at the camera or out into the scene, never at the screen.
Unless the user's prompt explicitly requests a different style (e.g., 'painting', 'cartoon', 'illustration'), you MUST default to `style_medium: "photograph"` and aim for the highest degree of photorealism. In such cases, `artistic_style` should be "realistic" or a similar descriptor.
The JSON object must contain the following keys precisely:
1.  `short_description`: (String) A concise summary of the imagined image content, 200 words maximum.
2.  `objects`: (Array of Objects) List the prominent objects of the scene. For each object, include:
    * `description`: (String) A detailed description of the imagined object, 100 words maximum.
    * `location`: (String) E.g., "center", "top-left", "bottom-right foreground".
    * `relative_size`: (String) E.g., "small", "medium", "large within frame". (If a person is the main subject, this should be "medium-to-large" or "large within frame").
    * `shape_and_color`: (String) Describe the basic shape and dominant color.
    * `texture`: (String) E.g., "smooth", "rough", "metallic", "furry".
    * `appearance_details`: (String) Any other notable visual details.
    * `relationship`: (String) Describe the relationship between the object and the other objects in the image.
    * `orientation`: (String) Describe the orientation or positioning of the object, e.g., "upright", "tilted 45 degrees", "horizontal", "vertical", "facing left", "facing right", "upside down", "lying on its side".
    * If the object is a human or a human-like object, include the following:
        * `pose`: (String) Describe the body position.
        * `expression`: (String) Describe facial expression and emotion. E.g., "winking", "joyful", "serious", "surprised", "calm".
        * `clothing`: (String) Describe attire.
        * `action`: (String) Describe the action of the human.
        * `gender`: (String) Describe the gender of the human.
        * `skin_tone_and_texture`: (String) Describe the skin tone and texture.
    * If the object is a cluster of objects, include the following:
        * `number_of_objects`: (Integer) The number of objects in the cluster.
3.  `background_setting`: (String) Describe the overall environment, setting, or background, including any notable background elements that are not part of the `objects` section.
4.  `lighting`: (Object)
    * `conditions`: (String) E.g., "bright daylight", "dim indoor", "studio lighting", "golden hour".
    * `direction`: (String) E.g., "front-lit", "backlit", "side-lit from left".
    * `shadows`: (String) Describe the presence and quality of shadows, e.g., "long, soft shadows", "sharp, defined shadows", "minimal shadows".
5.  `aesthetics`: (Object)
    * `composition`: (String) E.g., "rule of thirds", "symmetrical", "centered", "leading lines". If people are the main subject, specify the shot type, e.g., "medium shot", "close-up", "portrait composition".
    * `color_scheme`: (String) E.g., "monochromatic blue", "warm complementary colors", "high contrast".
    * `mood_atmosphere`: (String) E.g., "serene", "energetic", "mysterious", "joyful".
6.  `photographic_characteristics`: (Object)
    * `depth_of_field`: (String) E.g., "shallow", "deep", "bokeh background".
    * `focus`: (String) E.g., "sharp focus on subject", "soft focus", "motion blur".
    * `camera_angle`: (String) E.g., "eye-level", "low angle", "high angle", "dutch angle".
    * `lens_focal_length`: (String) E.g., "wide-angle", "telephoto", "macro", "fisheye". (If the main subject is a person, prefer "standard lens (e.g., 35mm-50mm)" or "portrait lens (e.g., 50mm-85mm)" to ensure they are framed more closely. Avoid "wide-angle" for people unless specified).
7.  `style_medium`: (String) Identify the artistic style or medium based on the user's prompt or creative interpretation (e.g., "photograph", "oil painting", "watercolor", "3D render", "digital illustration", "pencil sketch").
8.  `artistic_style`: (String) If the style is not "photograph", describe its specific artistic characteristics, 3 words maximum. (e.g., "impressionistic, vibrant, textured" for an oil painting).
9.  `context`: (String) Provide a general description of the type of image this would be. For example: "This is a concept for a high-fashion editorial photograph intended for a magazine spread," or "This describes a piece of concept art for a fantasy video game."
10. `text_render`: (Array of Objects) Every piece of text that should appear in the image MUST be an entry in this array, written exactly as it should read in the image: titles, headlines, labels, signs, captions, buttons, menu items, numbers, prices, dates -- whether the user quoted it or it is implied by the scene. Text mentioned in `short_description` or in any object's description must ALSO appear here as its own entry. Put each separate line, label or list item in its own entry. If the image has no text, the array is empty (`[]`).
    * `text`: (String) The exact text as it should appear in the image. NEVER use generic placeholders.
    * `location`: (String) E.g., "center", "top-left", "bottom-right foreground".
    * `size`: (String) E.g., "medium", "large", "large within frame".
    * `color`: (String) E.g., "red", "blue", "green".
    * `font`: (String) E.g., "realistic", "cartoonish", "minimalist", "serif typeface".
    * `appearance_details`: (String) Any other notable visual details.
Ensure the information within the JSON is detailed, creative, internally consistent, and avoids redundancy between fields.
The user's message is the request. Generate a detailed JSON object, adhering to the expected schema, for an imagined scene based on that request.

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 These FIBO 2 workflows need ComfyUI 0.43.0 or newer, the first version with FIBO 2. We made and tested them on 0.45.2. On an older ComfyUI some nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download fibo2_edit_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors8.41 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/fibo2

Create the fibo2 folder if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP (FIBO 2 text encoder)

Download qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors8.88 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load CLIP (the JSON helper)

Download qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors9.35 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

The small language model that writes the JSON. The same file as ComfyUI's own FIBO 2 templates use.

 Load VAE

Download flux2-vae.safetensors336 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

The Flux 2 VAE, the same download as in our Flux 2 and FLUX 3 Klein workflows: if you have flux2-vae.safetensors from those, you already have it.

 License

FIBO 2 is made by Bria AI. It is free for personal and non-commercial use under the CC BY-NC 4.0 license. To use the pictures commercially, you need a license from Bria.

BRIA LICENSE AND PRICING FIBO 2 model page 

The JSON helper follows Bria's own instructions from their open VGL toolkit (MIT license): github.com/Bria-AI/vgl. Thank you, Bria.

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.250). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Type a short idea and get a photo from FIBO 2, the image model by Bria. FIBO 2 was trained on long, structured descriptions written as JSON, a list of every object, the light, the camera and the words to draw. So AI Prompt Pixaroma runs a small helper model that writes that JSON from your idea first, following Bria's own instructions, and FIBO 2 Turbo draws it in 4 steps.

 Steps

  1. Type your idea in AI Prompt Pixaroma (1).
  2. Pick a size on Sizes Pixaroma (2): all five are about 1 megapixel, the size FIBO 2 was made for.
  3. Leave the seed (3) on F to repeat a picture, or switch it to R for a new one each Run.
  4. Press Run. The JSON the helper wrote shows in the box under your idea.

 Writing a short idea

  • One line is enough: who, what they are doing, where, and the light. A close-up portrait of a smiling woman pouring maple syrup on a stack of pancakes at her kitchen counter ...
  • Words that must appear in the picture go in double quotes: a white mug with "PIXA" on it. FIBO 2 is very good at text.
  • The helper fills in the rest by itself: the kitchen, her clothes, the plate, the window light. Read its JSON to see what it chose.
  • Want a cleaner picture? Keep it close and the room calm, as in the demo: a simple uncluttered kitchen. A wide, busy shop gave us things floating in the air. You can also say no other characters, simple background, or empty, no people.

 Good to know

  • Turbo changes little between seeds. In our tests the four seeds gave almost the same picture. For a different picture, change a few words of the idea, or use workflow 2 (Dev), where every seed looks different.
  • The same idea gives the same JSON every Run, so a new seed only redraws the picture, in about 2 seconds.
  • Look at the hands at full size. In 2 of our 4 Turbo seeds she held the syrup bottle by a stick that went into it. A new seed fixes it in 2 seconds.
  • Read the JSON when something looks wrong. In one test the helper wrote a bunny logo as the words "Orange Bunny Logo", and Turbo printed those words on the apron. Changing the idea fixes it, or workflow 3 changes one thing for you.
  • Small figures far away (fairies, birds, a crowd) come out soft at this size: FIBO 2 makes about 1 megapixel, so a figure 60 pixels tall has little room for a face. Ask for them closer, or leave them out.
  • Keep to these sizes. FIBO 2 was trained at about 1 megapixel; ComfyUI's notes say a much bigger size makes it follow the description worse.
  • Leave the formula on AI Prompt Pixaroma as it is: it holds Bria's instructions. Its Faster writing (MTP) switch is off, so the JSON repeats exactly.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

What AI Prompt needs Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (FIBO 2 Turbo) - FIBO 2 Turbo by Bria: the fast version, 4 steps. The file is called edit turbo, but it makes new pictures too.
  • Load CLIP (FIBO 2 text encoder) - Reads the JSON description for FIBO 2: Qwen3-VL 4B. The type must be fibo2.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2 VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. FIBO 2 uses the Flux 2 VAE, the same file as our Flux 2 and FLUX 3 Klein workflows.
  • Load CLIP (the JSON helper, Qwen3-VL 8B) - The JSON helper: Qwen3-VL 8B, a small language model that can see pictures. It is wired into AI Prompt Pixaroma, which uses it to write the long JSON description FIBO 2 was trained on. The type must be fibo2.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • AI Prompt Pixaroma (1. your idea, the helper writes the JSON) - Type your short idea here. The helper turns it into the long JSON description FIBO 2 was trained on, following Bria's own instructions (in the formula, sent as a system message), and shows the JSON in the box below. Its seed stays on F, so the same idea gives the same JSON every Run. Want a simple scene? Say it in the idea: no other characters, simple background.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. picture size) - The picture size. All five are the sizes FIBO 2 was trained at, about 1 megapixel each: square, 5:4, 4:3, 3:2 and 16:9. The Portrait / Landscape switch turns them on their side. The demo is 4:3 in portrait, 864 x 1152.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. fixed or random) - The picture's seed. F (fixed) gives the same picture every Run, R (random) a new one each Run. The demo uses seed 4. It does not change the JSON: the helper has its own seed, on AI Prompt Pixaroma.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Fibo 2 (JSON + size) - Reads the JSON description and makes the empty canvas in the size from Sizes Pixaroma.
  • KSampler (4 steps, CFG 1) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler and simple, the settings Bria publishes for Turbo.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the picture) - Saves each picture as PNG into ComfyUI/output/FIBO 2 Text to Image and shows it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds.

WhatTime
The helper writing the JSON15 to 20 s
The picture, 864 x 1152, 4 stepsabout 2 s
One Run with a new idea, start to endabout 20 s
A new seed, same ideaabout 2 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 27 GB: 8.4 GB for FIBO 2, 8.9 GB for the text encoder, 9.4 GB for the JSON helper and 0.3 GB for the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it.

 On a smaller card

FIBO 2 makes pictures of about 1 megapixel, so the picture size is not what makes it heavy: the three models are. ComfyUI moves what does not fit on the card into your PC's memory, which is slower. The same Hugging Face folders also hold smaller versions of both text encoders (int8 for the FIBO 2 one, fp8 and smaller for the helper); we tested only the files in Model Downloads.
